notation.title: Scale and round a measurement
notation.intro: Adjust a normalized coefficient and an integer power of ten. Compare standard form, decimal value, decimal-place rounding and significant figures.
notation.working: 0.00072 = 7.2 × 10⁻⁴; a normalized positive coefficient is at least 1 and below 10.

geometric.title: Compare geometric terms and totals
geometric.intro: Change the first term and common ratio, including negative ratios. The table is a finite sequence; its sum is not an infinite series.
geometric.challenge: Find the sum of the first five terms of 3, 6, 12, … .
geometric.working: 3 + 6 + 12 + 24 + 48 = 93. In sigma notation this is Σ from k=0 to 4 of 3 × 2ᵏ.

finance.title: Include inflation and depreciation
finance.intro: Compare nominal savings, purchasing power and a depreciating asset. The annual savings rate is nominal, compounded m times per year; inflation and depreciation are annual effective rates. No fees or taxes.
finance.challenge: An asset worth 1000 loses 10% of its value each year. Find its value after two years.
finance.working: 1000 × 0.9² = 810. Purchasing power of savings is nominal balance divided by (1 + inflation rate)ᵗ.

logarithms.title: Undo an exponential
logarithms.intro: Explore exponent laws for integer exponents and logarithms as inverse operations. Select base 10 or e for the graph. The integer-base calculation below uses base 2.
logarithms.working: 10⁻³ = 0.001, so log₁₀(0.001) = −3. Logarithms require positive arguments.

bounds.title: Turn rounding into an interval
bounds.intro: Set a measured radius and its rounding unit. Investigate the resulting bounds on circle area and the largest relative discrepancy from the area calculated using the reported radius.
bounds.challenge: A length is 8.4 cm to the nearest 0.1 cm. Find its lower bound.
bounds.working: Half the rounding unit is 0.05: 8.35 ≤ length < 8.45 cm. State bounds before rounding a derived result.

annuity.title: Build an end-of-period annuity
annuity.intro: Deposit a fixed amount at the end of each month. Compare contributions with interest earned. Interest is applied before each new deposit; no fees or taxes.
annuity.challenge: Deposit 100 at each year-end with 10% annual interest. What is the balance just after the second deposit?
annuity.working: The first deposit grows to 110; the second deposit adds 100. Total 210, because the second deposit has not yet earned interest.

systems.title: Solve a three-variable system
systems.intro: Move the three right-hand sides of x + y + z = A, x − y + z = B, and x + y − z = C. A technology-style solver finds a unique solution and displays residuals.
systems.challenge: For x+y+z=6, x−y+z=2 and x+y−z=0, find z.
systems.working: Subtract the third equation from the first: 2z = 6, so z = 3. Then y = 2 and x = 1.

polynomials.title: Locate polynomial roots and intersections
polynomials.intro: Move q in f(x) = x³ − 3x and the horizontal line g(x) = q. The solver reports all real intersections in the displayed interval, including tangent intersections at q = ±2. Gold is g; mint is f.
polynomials.challenge: How many distinct real solutions does x³ − 3x = 0 have?
polynomials.working: x(x² − 3) = 0 gives −√3, 0, √3. A plotted crossing is a root of f(x) − q.

inverse.title: Restrict a domain and undo a function
inverse.intro: Use f(x) = 2x + 3 on a closed input interval. Compare its graph with its inverse and the reflection line y = x. Domain restrictions carry over to the inverse's range.
inverse.working: Undo +3, then divide by 2: (11 − 3)/2 = 4. An inverse reverses input and output; it is not a reciprocal.

graph-operations.title: Add graphs and inspect their features
graph-operations.intro: Compare f(x)=x²−4, g(x)=mx+b, their sum and their difference. Predict intercepts and sketch the selected graph on paper with labelled axes before revealing its features.
graph-operations.working: f(2)=0 and g(2)=2, so their sum is 2. Subtracting graphs instead gives −2.

model-family.title: Choose and test a model family
model-family.intro: Explore linear tariffs, exponential change, power laws, cubics and periodic models. Adjust parameters and compare with fictional data. A low residual alone does not justify extrapolation; use the stated context and domain.
choices: Tariff: ax up to 2, then 2a + b(x−2)
model-family.challenge: A seasonal model is y = 4 sin(30x°) + 10. Find its period.
model-family.working: Period = 360/30 = 12; amplitude 4; principal axis y=10. A periodic model is suitable for repeating seasonal behaviour, not unlimited growth.

solids.title: Measure a three-dimensional solid
solids.intro: Compare volume and total external surface area. In a rectangular prism, inspect the space diagonal and the midpoint between opposite vertices. All lengths are in the same unit.
solids.working: √(3²+4²+12²) = 13. The midpoint is (1.5,2,6). Right-angled triangles also determine diagonals and slant heights of solids.

nonright.title: Solve a non-right triangle
nonright.intro: Move two sides and their included angle. Compare the cosine-rule third side, sine-rule angles and area. Also inspect a fixed SSA example with two possible triangles.
nonright.challenge: Two sides are 6 and 8 with included angle 30°. Find the area.
nonright.working: Area = ½ × 6 × 8 × sin30° = 12. In SSA data, check the supplementary sine-rule angle as well as the acute solution.

bearings.title: Navigate using a bearing
bearings.intro: A bearing is measured clockwise from north. Move a journey length and bearing to resolve east and north displacement and find the reverse bearing.
bearings.challenge: What is the reverse bearing of 070°?
bearings.working: Add 180° and reduce modulo 360°: 070° → 250°. Draw north lines and label your triangle; a bearing is not an angle measured from the east axis.

sectors.title: Open a circular sector
sectors.intro: Change a radius and central angle in degrees. Compare arc length, area and the perimeter of the sector (arc plus two radii).
sectors.challenge: Find the arc length of a 90° sector of radius 4. Give a decimal answer.
sectors.working: (90/360) × 2π × 4 = 2π ≈ 6.28319. Sector area uses the same angular fraction of πr².

bisectors.title: Construct a perpendicular bisector
bisectors.intro: Move B while A stays at (0,0). Display the midpoint and the perpendicular bisector in standard form, which also handles vertical boundaries.
bisectors.challenge: The points are (0,0) and (6,0). Find the x-coordinate of every point on their perpendicular bisector.
bisectors.working: The midpoint is (3,0). The joining segment is horizontal, so the perpendicular bisector is the vertical line x=3.

sampling.title: Audit a sampling method
sampling.intro: A fictional population has 60 younger and 40 older members, with group mean scores 40 and 70. Compare expected sample composition across methods; this is a design comparison, not random data generation.
sampling.challenge: In a proportional sample of 20 from a population that is 40% older, how many older members should be sampled?
sampling.working: 20 × 0.4 = 8. Stratified sampling randomly samples within groups; filling quotas by convenience can still introduce bias.

displays.title: Link frequency, quartiles and outliers
displays.intro: Use equal-width classes [0,10), [10,20), [20,30), [30,40). Move one frequency and compare a histogram, cumulative frequency and a box plot of the midpoint-coded data. Grouped estimates are not exact raw-data values.
displays.challenge: For ordered data 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 using medians of the lower and upper halves, find the interquartile range.
displays.working: Q1=2.5 and Q3=6.5, so IQR=4. Outlier fences are Q1−1.5IQR and Q3+1.5IQR. A valid unusual observation should not automatically be deleted.

events.title: Build an event table and probability tree
events.intro: Adjust four disjoint regions of a 100-person population. Compare a union, intersection and conditional probability. Then inspect a two-draw tree without replacement from a bag with 3 red and 2 blue counters.
events.challenge: A bag contains 3 red and 2 blue counters. Draw twice without replacement. Find P(two red).
events.working: P(RR) = 3/5 × 2/4 = 0.3. The second probability changes because the first counter is not replaced.

expectation.title: Price a discrete game fairly
expectation.intro: Win 0, 5 or 20 credits. Change the probability of the top prize and entry fee. The 5-credit outcome has probability 0.30; the zero prize takes the remaining probability.
expectation.challenge: Prizes 0, 5, 20 have probabilities 0.6, 0.3, 0.1. Find a fair entry fee.
expectation.working: E(prize)=0(0.6)+5(0.3)+20(0.1)=3.5. A fee of 3.5 gives expected net gain zero, not a guaranteed zero gain on each play.

inverse-normal.title: Find a percentile and an interval
inverse-normal.intro: Set a normal mean and standard deviation and move the cumulative percentile. The cutoff is found numerically. Compare the probability within one standard deviation of the mean.
inverse-normal.challenge: For a normal distribution with mean 100, what is its 50th percentile?
inverse-normal.working: The median equals the mean by symmetry. Inverse normal calculations start with an area and find its boundary value.

rank.title: Rank data with tied values
rank.intro: Change the final observation in the pairs (1,1),(2,2),(3,2),(4,4),(5,y). Compare Pearson correlation with correlation of the average ranks. Tied ranks are averaged.
rank.challenge: Two observations occupy rank positions 2 and 3 and are tied. What rank is assigned to each?
rank.working: Each receives (2+3)/2 = 2.5. Pearson measures linear association; Spearman measures monotonic association and is generally less sensitive to extreme magnitudes.

chi-square.title: Test categorical data with chi-square
chi-square.intro: Compare observations with expectations. Independence mode uses two groups and three choices (df=2); goodness-of-fit mode uses three equally likely outcomes (df=2). These teaching tables keep every expected count above 5.
chi-square.challenge: For a 2-by-3 contingency table, what are the degrees of freedom?
chi-square.working: df=(2−1)(3−1)=2. For goodness of fit to three specified category probabilities, df=3−1=2. Compare p to α; failing to reject is not proof of H₀.

t-test.title: Compare two independent means
t-test.intro: Use the pooled two-sample t-test for independent samples from normal populations with unknown but equal variances. Both sample sizes are 10 and group B's mean is 50. Choose the alternative before interpreting p.
t-test.challenge: Two independent samples each have size 10. Find the pooled t-test degrees of freedom.
t-test.working: df=nA+nB−2=18. H₀ states equal population means; the alternative determines which tail or tails contribute to p.

power-rule.title: Differentiate an integer-power model
power-rule.intro: Explore f(x)=axⁿ+bx+c and its derivative for positive and negative integer n. The graph stays on x>0 so negative powers are defined. Mint is f; gold is f′.
power-rule.working: f′(x)=9x²−2, so f′(2)=36−2=34. A constant differentiates to zero.

normal-line.title: Build a tangent and its normal
normal-line.intro: Move the point on y=x². Compare tangent and normal equations, including the vertical normal when the tangent is horizontal. Gold is the normal; mint is the tangent.
normal-line.challenge: For y=x² at x=1, find the slope of the normal.
normal-line.working: Tangent slope is 2. Perpendicular slopes multiply to −1, so the normal slope is −1/2. Its equation is y−1=−0.5(x−1).

antiderivative.title: Recover a function and accumulate area
antiderivative.intro: Given F′(x)=axⁿ, choose F(1) to determine the constant. Compare a definite integral over positive bounds. The choices omit n=−1, whose antiderivative is beyond this SL power-rule requirement.
antiderivative.challenge: F′(x)=2x and F(1)=5. Find the constant C in F(x)=x²+C.
antiderivative.working: 5=1+C gives C=4. The definite integral from 1 to 3 of 2x is F(3)−F(1)=8; C cancels.

stationary.title: Classify stationary points by sign
stationary.intro: Explore f(x)=x³−3ax. Move a and inspect where the derivative changes sign. Distinguish a stationary point of inflection from a local extremum without using a second-derivative test.
stationary.challenge: For f(x)=x³−3x, find the x-coordinate of the local minimum.
stationary.working: f′=3x²−3 vanishes at ±1. Its sign changes from negative to positive at x=1, so this is a local minimum. At x=−1 it changes positive to negative, giving a local maximum.

box-transform.title: Transform and compare box plots
box-transform.intro: Change one extreme observation, then transform every value using y=ax+b. Compare the original and transformed distributions and investigate the 1.5 IQR outlier rule. Quartiles use medians of halves, excluding the middle observation.
box-transform.challenge: A data set has mean 7 and population variance 16. Each value is multiplied by 3 and then increased by 2. Find the new variance.
box-transform.working: Multiplication by 3 multiplies variance by 3²; adding a constant does not change spread. New variance = 9 × 16 = 144; new mean = 23.

voronoi-regions.title: Add a site and measure Voronoi cells
voronoi-regions.intro: Explore exact clipped Voronoi regions inside a 10 by 10 map. Add or remove site C and move it. Inspect the areas and a vertex shared by three regions. A=(2,2), B=(8,2); C moves above them.
voronoi-regions.challenge: Two service sites at (2,2) and (8,2) serve a square map 0≤x≤10, 0≤y≤10. What is the area nearest A?
voronoi-regions.working: The boundary is x=5, so the left rectangle has area 5 × 10 = 50. With additional sites, clip each region by its pairwise bisectors.
